newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge jails soccer hooligans for murder.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge jails soccer hooligans for murder.

text.p: An Argentine judge on Friday jailed five soccer hooligans, all fans of Boca Juniors, for up to 20 years for the murder of two fans of rival Buenos Aires side River Plate in 1994.

But Argentina's most notorious soccer hooligan, Jose Barrita, alias "The Grandfather", had already been cleared of the double homicide charge and was jailed for 13 years on Friday for heading an illegal organisation and racketeering.

Barrita, ex-leader of the Boca "Barra Brava" -- the local term for soccer gangs which translates as "Wild Bunch" -- was also let off charges of demanding "protection money" from people operating concessions in the Boca stadium.

Two River Plate fans died in an ambush by pistol-toting Boca fans following a local derby in April 1994. One was shot dead and another was run over after falling out of a truck. Three more River fans received serious gunshot wounds.
Prosecutors had demanded life sentences for seven of the nine Boca fans on trial since March. But as well as Barrita, two were let off the murder charges and given lesser terms.
